summary: Solid, production-plausible CDC architecture using Debezium/Kafka as the durability and replay boundary, with downstream idempotent upserts keyed by a monotonic source position to achieve exactly-once effects. It covers core operational needs (control plane, schema registry, DLQ, observability) and acknowledges key failure modes, but leaves some hard correctness and destination-specific implementation details underspecified.
strengths: Clear correctness story (log as source of truth, Kafka replay, idempotent upserts using commit positions) with pragmatic at-least-once delivery.
Good operational framing: control plane APIs, schema evolution workflow, DLQ strategy, and concrete SLO/throughput targets plus failure-mode handling.
weaknesses: Exactly-once effects rely on correct partitioning/keying and per-destination merge semantics; multi-table transactions/atomicity and cross-partition ordering are not fully resolved beyond metadata.

Destination specifics (Snowflake/BigQuery/Redshift MERGE patterns, Iceberg/Delta/Hudi upsert/compaction strategies, concurrency limits, and cost/perf tuning) are high-level given the stated scale (5–20 TB/day).
